chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abdillah ibn Ahmad, from 'Umar ibn Sahl, from 'ibn Sahl, from 'Ali ibn Musahir al-Qurashi, who said:

My grandmother told me that she was alive at the time of the killing of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). She said, 'We remained for one year and nine months, and the sky was like a clot of blood, like blood; we could not see the sun.'

key_terms.أَدْرَكَتْ: She was alive and contemporary with
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Imam al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (a.s.), grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.الْعَلَقَةُ: A clot of blood (referring to the stage of fetal development, used here for color/texture)

ai.seo_question: What were the signs in the sky after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmological dimension of the martyrdom, where the prolonged redness of the sky symbolizes the heavens' grief. It reflects the Shia belief in the interconnectedness of the spiritual and physical realms, where the death of the Imam affects the entire creation, serving as a sign for believers to reflect on the cosmic impact of Ahl al-Bayt's trials.
